issue: Node falsely credits Marguerite Harl as 'co-éditrice (avec Doutreleau) des Homélies sur la Genèse d'Origène (SC 7bis, Cerf 1976, rééd.)'. SC 7/7bis (Origène, Homélies sur la Genèse) was edited, translated and annotated by Louis Doutreleau alone (Latin text after Rufinus' version), with an introduction by Henri de Lubac and Doutreleau. Harl is not listed as editor or co-editor.
evidence: Co-éditrice (avec Doutreleau) des Homélies sur la Genèse d'Origène (SC 7bis, Cerf 1976, rééd.)
current: Helléniste française (1919-2020), professeur à Paris-Sorbonne, fondatrice de la Bible d'Alexandrie (traduction française commentée de la Septante, Cerf, série dirigée à partir de 1986). Pivot de la réception française d'Origène — éditrice de la Philocalie 1-20 d'Origène (SC 302, Cerf 1983). Ouvrage de référence : Origène et la fonction révélatrice du Verbe incarné (Patristica Sorbonensia 2, Seuil 1958). Co-éditrice (avec Doutreleau) des Homélies sur la Genèse d'Origène (SC 7bis, Cerf 1976, rééd.). Son école a formé une génération de patristiciens français du judéo-grec.
proposed: Helléniste française (1919-2020), professeur à Paris-Sorbonne, fondatrice de la Bible d'Alexandrie (traduction française commentée de la Septante, Cerf, série dirigée à partir de 1986). issue: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite is a genuinely anonymous author whose actual birth and death dates are unknown. The only dateable fact is the floruit / composition date c. 500 CE (the Corpus Areopagiticum is dated c. 500 via its dependence on Proclus). Setting both birth_date and death_date to 'c. 500 CE' falsely implies known biographical dates and a near-zero lifespan, when scholarship uniformly treats c. 500 CE as a floruit, not as birth/death years.
proposed: birth_date=null, death_date=null (author is anonymous; birth/death unknown). The floruit c. 500 CE is already correctly stated in the node description; it should not be encoded as biographical birth/death dates.
sources: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, article titled 'Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite (fl. 500 CE)' (https://iep.utm.edu/pseudodi/) — uses 'fl.' (floruit), not birth/death dates; identity unknown

Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite' (https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/pseudo-dionysius-areopagite/) — corpus dated c. 500 CE via dependence on Proclus; author identity an unsolved mystery
Britannica, 'Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite' (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Pseudo-Dionysius-the-Areopagite) — anonymous author, c. 500 CE
rationale: The scanner is correct. Authoritative scholarship (IEP, SEP, Britannica) is unanimous that the author is anonymous with unknown birth/death dates, and that c. 500 CE is a floruit/composition date, not a lifespan. Encoding identical birth_date=death_date='c. 500 CE' is a false-fact: it asserts biographical dates that are not known and implies an impossible ~0-year life. The grounded correction is to null both fields; the floruit remains accurately represented in the description. Fix is scholarly (factual content), severity medium (imprecise/false but on a node where the floruit itself is correct and prominently stated).

issue: Two distinct bibliographic errors in the same description string. (A) [this pass] GNO vol. II (Pars Altera = Contra Eunomium Liber III + Refutatio Confessionis Eunomii) is dated '1925'; its editio princeps was Berlin: Weidmann 1921, concurrent with GNO vol. I (Books I-II, also 1921), revised 1960 (Brill, Leiden), with a later 1990 Brill reprint — there was no intermediate 1925 edition. (B) [prior pass, retained] The NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 5 English translation of Against Eunomius is attributed to S.G. Hall, but the actual NPNF 2.5 translators were W. Moore, H.A. Wilson, and H.C. Ogle (ed. Schaff-Wace, 1893); Hall's translation is the modern Brill Supplements to Vigiliae Christianae colloquium volumes, a distinct series.
evidence: Description: 'Critical edition: W. Jaeger, GNO I (Books I and II; 1921, rev. 1960), GNO II (Book III; 1925, rev. 1960; Brill 1990 reprint). English: S.G. Hall (in NPNF 2.5; ...).' Internet Archive scan 'contraeunomiumli02greg' (= GNO II Pars Altera) bears the imprint 'Berolini: Apud Weidmannos, 1921'. NPNF 2.5 'Against Eunomius' translators = Moore/Wilson/Ogle (CCEL npnf205; New Advent 2901).
current: GNO II (Book III; 1925, rev. 1960; Brill 1990 reprint). English: S.G. Hall (in NPNF 2.5)
proposed: GNO II (Book III; 1921, rev. 1960; Brill 1990 reprint). English: W. Moore, H.A. Wilson, and H.C. Ogle (in NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 5, ed. Schaff-Wace, 1893); a modern critical English translation by S.G. Hall appears in the Brill 'Supplements to Vigiliae Christianae' colloquium volumes (CE II, ed. Karfíková, vol. 82, 2007; CE III, ed. Leemans-Cassin, vol. 124, 2014; CE I, ed. Brugarolas, vol. 148, 2018)
rationale: Both sub-claims independently confirmed against primary metadata, not memory. (A) GNO II date: Internet Archive scan 'contraeunomiumli02greg' carries the title-page imprint 'Berolini: Apud Weidmannos, 1921'; Brill GNO serial page, HathiTrust, abebooks, and the Rutgers DBCS Jaeger biography all give 1921 (Berlin) as the editio princeps of GNO I and II, with the 1960 second edition by Brill (Leiden). No 1925 edition of this volume exists; the date is a single-token error. (B) NPNF translators: CCEL npnf205 and New Advent 2901 attribute 'Against Eunomius' to W. Moore, H.A. Wilson, H.C. Ogle (1893); S.G. Hall is the translator in Brill's Supplements to Vigiliae Christianae (CE II = SVC 82, 2007; CE III = SVC 124, 2014; CE I = SVC 148, 2018). The two series are conflated. Both corrections are grounded and warrant a scholarly fix; fix_class=scholarly governs the merged finding.

issue: The description states '71 sections (counting Ambigua 6–71 in the traditional numbering)'. Counting the difficulties numbered 6 through 71 yields 66 sections (71 − 6 + 1 = 66), not 71. The figure 71 is the highest ambiguum number in the combined corpus (Ambigua ad Thomam 1–5 + Ambigua ad Iohannem 6–71), not the count of sections in the Ambigua ad Iohannem. The current phrasing is internally contradictory.
evidence: current text: '71 sections (counting Ambigua 6–71 in the traditional numbering; preceded by Ambigua ad Thomam, 5 sections)'. The same sentence already states the predecessor work has 5 sections (Ambigua 1–5 = ad Thomam), so the ad Iohannem necessarily spans Amb. 6–71 = 66 difficulties. The standard structure (Amb. 1–5 = ad Thomam; Amb. 6–71 = ad Iohannem) is the uncontested numbering used in the Constas critical edition (Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library 28–29, Harvard 2014).
current: 71 sections (counting Ambigua 6–71 in the traditional numbering)
proposed: 66 sections (Ambigua 6–71 in the traditional numbering, where Ambigua 1–5 = Ambigua ad Thomam)
rationale: Arithmetic is unambiguous: difficulties numbered 6 through 71 inclusive = 66 sections. The combined Ambigua corpus comprises the Ambigua ad Thomam (Amb. 1–5) plus the Ambigua ad Iohannem (Amb. 6–71); this two-part structure with the 5 + 66 split is standard in Maximian scholarship and in the Constas edition cited in the node itself. The '71' refers to the last ambiguum number, not the section count. The node already correctly states the ad Thomam has 5 sections, making the '71' figure self-contradictory. Correction is grounded in the edition already cited; no ancient text composed.
sources: Nicholas Constas (ed./trans.), On Difficulties in the Church Fathers: The Ambigua, Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library 28–29 (Harvard University Press, 2014) — vol. I = Ambigua ad Thomam + Ambigua ad Iohannem 1–22; vol. II = Ambigua to John 23–71

issue: The node attributes the 1996 original edition of 'Les Stoïciens et l'âme' to Vrin. The 1996 original was published by PUF (Presses Universitaires de France) in the collection 'Philosophies' (ISBN 2130478085). Vrin published only the 2017 reissue (ISBN 9782711627752). The node collapses both editions under 'Vrin, 1996', misattributing the original publisher.
evidence: Node description: '*Les Stoïciens et l'âme* (Vrin, 1996 ; nouvelle édition 2017)'. Confirmed via Amazon.fr listing for ISBN 2130478085 (PUF, coll. Philosophies, 1996), the Persée review (Revue des études anciennes 1997) citing 'Philosophie; 75' (a PUF series number), and French Wikipedia: 'Original publication: P.U.F., Paris, 1996; Reissue: Vrin, Paris, 2nd edition 2017'.

proposed: Les Stoïciens et l'âme (PUF, « Philosophies », 1996 ; réédition Vrin, 2017)
rationale: Three independent authoritative sources confirm the 1996 original is PUF ('Philosophies', ISBN 2130478085) and the 2017 reissue is Vrin (ISBN 9782711627752). The scanner's correction is exactly right. Fix is scholarly (bibliographic attribution).
